topStories.headline: Retirement Community at Julia Morgan's Marina Landmark Files Expanded Eight-Story Addition
topStories.dek: Heritage on the Marina and Sequoia Living have filed revised plans for a major expansion behind the 1925 landmarked Julia Morgan Building at 3400 Laguna Street.
topStories.body:
An ambitious redevelopment of one of the Marina District's most architecturally significant sites took a new step this week when updated plans were filed for the Heritage on the Marina retirement community at 3400 Laguna Street. The latest application, filed by Heritage on the Marina and nonprofit senior housing provider Sequoia Living, seeks to add an eight-story complex directly behind the landmarked three-story brick facility designed by the celebrated Beaux-Arts architect Julia Morgan.

Once complete, the two-structure development would span approximately 196,700 square feet, including 134,180 square feet of residential space. The historic Morgan Building — a Jacobethan Revival structure completed in 1925 for the San Francisco Ladies' Protection and Relief Society and designated a city landmark in December 2024 — would retain ten apartments. The new eight-story tower would house 112 independent living units and eight assisted living suites. A basement garage would provide space for 29 cars and 46 bicycles.

The project represents a significant scale-up from earlier proposals. A 2024 environmental review had envisioned growing the campus from roughly 83,200 to 141,580 square feet, but the newest filing pushes the total footprint considerably higher. HKIT Architects is overseeing the design of both the new construction and alterations to the historic building, while preservation firm Page & Turnbull will supervise work on the landmarked structure.

The expansion would require demolition of two existing connector buildings while preserving the Morgan Building as the campus focal point, visually separated from its modern addition. The project still requires city planning approvals and historic preservation review before construction could begin.

topStories.headline: Presidio Marks Its 250th Birthday September 17 with Film Premiere and Champagne Reception
topStories.dek: The Presidio Historical Association and SF Historical Society will celebrate the park's exact founding anniversary with a world-premiere documentary screening at the historic Presidio Theatre.
topStories.body:
On September 17, 2026 — the exact 250th anniversary of the founding of El Presidio de San Francisco — the Presidio Historical Association and the San Francisco Historical Society will present the world premiere of 'Anza 250: A Documentary Film' at the beautifully restored, 600-seat Presidio Theatre at 99 Moraga Avenue.

The film chronicles Professor Luis Valle's remarkable bicycle journey retracing the Anza Expedition's 1,200-mile route from present-day Sonora, Mexico, to the Presidio — the same path that led to the establishment of the Spanish outpost on September 17, 1776, while the Declaration of Independence was being signed on the East Coast. Doors open at 5:30 p.m. with a raffle; a champagne reception for the Presidio's birthday will follow the screening.

The anniversary is the centerpiece of a broader year of commemoration at the Presidio, which has been programming special cultural events throughout 2026 as part of the nationwide America 250 initiative. Earlier this summer, ArtSeed's 20th Annual Open Call Exhibition opened at the China Brotsky and Seed Galleries within the Presidio, and Mess Hall at the Presidio — a new all-day food hall led by James Beard Award-winning chef Peter Serpico — opened adjacent to Presidio Tunnel Tops at 201 Halleck Street.

The Presidio's story encompasses the Ramaytush Ohlone people who lived on the land for thousands of years before European contact, followed by Spanish and Mexican colonists, the United States Army, and finally its current role as a national park site. The Sept. 17 evening event is ticketed; details are available at presidiotheatre.org.

topStories.headline: Safeway Tower Opponents Weigh Legal Options as Planners Clear AB 2011 Hurdle
topStories.dek: With San Francisco planners confirming the Marina Safeway project meets state housing law eligibility, neighborhood groups are signaling that a lawsuit remains on the table.
topStories.body:
The week after San Francisco Planning Director Sarah Dennis Phillips ruled that the proposed mixed-use tower at 15 Marina Boulevard satisfies the eligibility requirements of California's AB 2011 housing streamlining law, opponents of the project are assessing their remaining options — and lawsuit threats are growing louder.

Phillips' ruling found that a city-owned parking lot across the street and Fort Mason's surrounding mix of parking, retail, and housing counted as urban uses under the statute's definition, clearing the largest remaining procedural hurdle for developer Align Real Estate. The project, designed by Arquitectonica, would replace the existing Marina Safeway with two conjoined residential towers — one 20 stories, one 18 stories — atop a larger replacement grocery store, totaling approximately 848 housing units.

With that ruling, District 2 Supervisor Stephen Sherrill and community groups have effectively exhausted their administrative options to block entitlement. As long as Align and Albertsons (which owns Safeway) comply with state law requirements — still being adjudicated by planners — the project is entitled to automatic approval. Opponents have not yet filed suit, but Lori Brooke, founder of Neighborhoods United SF, has publicly signaled that litigation remains possible, arguing that new state housing laws are 'colliding with complicated real-world conditions they were never anticipated or tested against,' according to the San Francisco Chronicle.

Supporters of the project argue the development would add badly needed housing in an area that has seen little multifamily construction for decades and would allow people priced out of the neighborhood to live in the Marina. The political divide over the tower has highlighted a generational and ideological rift in San Francisco housing politics that shows little sign of resolution.

moreNews.headline: Lobalita Cantina Brings Modern Mexican Cooking to Former Tipsy Pig Space
moreNews.body: A modern Mexican cantina called Lobalita opened in March 2026 at 2231 Chestnut Street, taking over the former Tipsy Pig space that closed in spring 2025 after 16 years. The project comes from hospitality veterans Stryker Scales, Nate Valentine, and Jamal Blake-Williams — the same group that opened the beloved gastropub — and features cocktails, tostadas, aguachile, and open-fire cooking led by chef Deiber Tzab. The low-lit interior includes a sprawling back patio, and all cocktails are priced at $14. The cantina is walk-in only with open seating, Tuesday through Sunday from 4 p.m.

moreNews.headline: Mess Hall at the Presidio Opens as All-Day Food Hall at Tunnel Tops
moreNews.body: Mess Hall at the Presidio has opened this summer as an all-day food hall inside a historic building at 201 Halleck Street, adjacent to Presidio Tunnel Tops. The concept — developed with James Beard Award-winning chef Peter Serpico — includes a café serving Wrecking Ball Coffee, a full cocktail, wine, and beer bar, a three-concept food hall leaning toward bread-based sandwiches, Korean-inspired fare, and seafood-centric plates, and a retail market, all with sweeping views of San Francisco Bay. The 6,200-square-foot venue in a former Army building is described as a permanent destination, not a pop-up.

moreNews.headline: Marina West Harbor Dredging: Second Round Planned for Fall
moreNews.body: Following completion of dredging that reopened the Marina's West Harbor after a large sandbar blocked access for months, the SF Recreation and Park Department has confirmed a second round of dredging is planned for the fall. The department continues to solicit public feedback on the broader Marina Improvement and Remediation project, which will ultimately go before the Recreation and Park Commission for approval with formal CEQA findings. Project updates are posted regularly at sfrecpark.org.

restaurants.name: Little Original Joe's

hotels.name: Pacific Heights Inn

hotels.name: Cow Hollow Inn & Suites
hotels.description: Comfortable Lombard Street motel offering spacious rooms and suites in the heart of Cow Hollow, with easy access to Union Street dining and the Marina waterfront.

hotels.name: Infinity Hotel San Francisco, Tapestry Collection by Hilton
hotels.description: Contemporary Marina hotel in the Tapestry Collection by Hilton, offering stylish rooms, a fitness center, and convenient access to Chestnut Street restaurants and the Presidio.

hotels.name: Jackson Court San Francisco
hotels.description: A charming ten-room inn housed in a historic 1900 Pacific Heights townhouse, offering understated elegance and a quiet retreat steps from Fillmore Street shopping.

shops.name: San Francisco Optics by Alexander Daas
shops.description: Family-owned eyewear shop on Chestnut Street for over 45 years, offering a curated selection of luxury frames and prescription lenses.

shops.name: Plumpjack Wine & Spirits

shops.description: Chestnut Street provisions shop specializing in artisan cheeses, charcuterie, imported pantry goods, and prepared foods for picnics and entertaining.

shops.name: Marin Country Mart – Starbucks / Crissy Field area
shops.description: The Crissy Field / Marina waterfront area anchored by healthy take-out options and small specialty grocers serving the cycling, hiking, and jogging community along the bay.
